releases.name: v0.7.0 - Coding Plan search and MCP session architecture
releases.body:
This release adds **Zhipu Coding Plan and Z.ai Coding Plan** search over Streamable HTTP MCP, bringing the total to **21 search channels**. It also separates MCP response parsing, search-result extraction, and session handling, with expanded automated verification and bilingual documentation.

### New search providers

- **Zhipu Coding Plan:** China Coding Plan search via `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/mcp/web_search_prime/mcp`, registered as `magpie-websearch:zhipu-coding`.
- **Z.ai Coding Plan:** International Coding Plan search via `https://api.z.ai/api/mcp/web_search_prime/mcp`, registered as `magpie-websearch:zai-coding`.
- Both providers require the corresponding site's Coding Plan key and consume shared plan credits. They remain separate from the existing Zhipu and Z.ai Standard REST providers, with independent credentials, configuration, endpoints, and caches.
- Search requests follow Magpie's requested result count and any explicit `resultLimit`. Optional recency, domain, and content-size fields are sent only when advertised by the server's tool schema; unsupported configured filters fail explicitly.

The Coding Plan providers are experimental. Real-account search and billing remain unverified on both sites, and Magpie's eligibility under the current client usage policy has not been confirmed. This project does not claim official Zhipu or Z.ai support for Magpie.

### Reliability and architecture

- Complete MCP session lifecycle on result-cache misses: `initialize`, `notifications/initialized`, `tools/list`, `tools/call`, and best-effort `DELETE`. Cache hits return results without opening a session.
- Initialization, discovery, and tool execution share one timeout budget; cleanup has a separate one-second limit. JSON and SSE responses, protocol negotiation, session headers, and host cancellation are supported.
- Preserve HTTP refusal status and validated `Retry-After` metadata while withholding refusal bodies and redacting known credentials and session identifiers. Session requests reject redirects.
- MCP failures never automatically switch to metered REST or retry on the other site. Magpie can still try another explicitly configured provider using that provider's own credentials.
- Organize MCP modules under `src/mcp/`, with independent stateless and session clients sharing response decoding. Parallel and TinyFish retain their direct, stateless MCP calls.
- Share search-result extraction with explicit per-caller compatibility options. Coding Plan supports structured content, `results` / `search_result` arrays, and up to three JSON decoding layers without broadening Parallel or TinyFish's default behavior.
- Read the MCP client version from the installed `package.json`, keeping handshake metadata aligned with the package.

### Documentation

- Update Chinese and English READMEs, technical references, provider guidance, and release checks for both Coding Plan channels.
- Clarify cache behavior, timeout boundaries, schema field gating, result URL filtering, and the distinction between provider isolation and Magpie's configured fallback.
- Add the README hero image and document MCP initialization metadata alongside the search-data privacy behavior.

### Validation

- **329 tests passed** on both Node.js 24.19.0 and Bun 1.4.4 across 26 test files.
- Isolated host checks passed on **Magpie 0.1.3141**, covering 21-channel registration, Coding Plan JSON/SSE sessions, schema-gated arguments, timeouts, key rotation, fallback, and site isolation.
- Release CI passed on **Node.js 22, Node.js 24, Bun, and the Magpie host smoke job**. Package dry-run checks include all MCP modules and both Coding Plan providers.
- Coding Plan validation uses dummy keys and local mock services; it does not establish real-account quota routing, billing, retrieval quality, or latency.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/guotree/magpie-websearch/compare/v0.6.1...v0.7.0

releases.name: v0.6.0 - Six new search providers and bilingual documentation alignment
releases.body:
This release adds **Perplexity, Bocha, Ollama, Jina, Kagi, and Serper**, bringing the total to **19 search APIs**. It also establishes full bilingual alignment across the documentation and configuration references, standardizes provider options ordering, and expands automated host verification.

### New search providers

- **Perplexity:** Official standalone Search API (`POST https://api.perplexity.ai/search`), supporting `web` and `fast` search modes, recency filtering, country and language filters, and local code-point truncation.
- **Bocha:** China standalone REST search API (`POST https://api.bochaai.com/v1/web-search`), default snippet mode with explicit opt-in for generated summaries (`summary: true`), freshness filters, and structured business error handling (`code`, `log_id`).
- **Ollama:** Official cloud Web Search API (`POST https://ollama.com/api/web_search`) requiring an Ollama account API key, with configurable content length budgets (`contentChars`) and URL filtering.
- **Jina:** Dedicated Jina Search API (`POST https://s.jina.ai/search`), default snippet mode with optional full-text extraction (`content: "full"`), `contentChars` truncation, and `gl`/`hl`/`location` parameter forwarding.
- **Kagi:** Kagi Search API in public preview (`POST https://kagi.com/api/v1/search`), with Lens override support, recency filtering (`day`/`week`/`month`), region filtering, and 1024 local result capping.
- **Serper:** Alternative Google organic search (`POST https://google.serper.dev/search`), fixed wire `num: 10`, local result capping via `maxResults`, `tbs` time filtering, and isolated `X-API-KEY` authentication independent of SerpApi.

All new providers integrate with Magpie's credential management, search ordering, and on/off controls, supporting custom complete endpoint URLs and per-provider options.

### Reliability and architecture

- Isolated credentials, endpoint routing, and per-provider caches across all 19 providers.
- Standardized `Retry-After` header parsing (delay-seconds or HTTP-date) and 429 key rest rotation across all newly added providers.
- Shared HTTP layer retains known HTTP status codes and retry metadata upon body consumption timeout or interruption, allowing Magpie to rotate to healthy keys.
- Independent options and environment variables per provider with full fallback behavior (`explicit option → environment variable → default`).

### Documentation

- Complete bilingual alignment between Chinese and English documentation (`README.md`, `README.en.md`, `docs/technical-reference.md`, `docs/technical-reference.en.md`).
- Symmetrically aligned Table 6 configuration reference covering all 113 options across 19 providers in alphabetical order.
- Synchronized CLI management commands, provider protocols table, and Table of Contents across both languages.
- Updated integration roadmap and status in `PROVIDERS.md` and verification guidelines in `RELEASING.md`.

### Validation

- **300 tests passed** on both Node.js 24.19.0 and Bun 1.4.4 across 22 test files.
- Isolated host checks passed on **Magpie 0.1.3041**, covering registration filters, custom exact endpoints, timeouts, 429 cooldown, key rotation, and fallback.
- New providers were verified with dummy keys and local mock services. Successful searches, billing, account limits, and retrieval quality with real account keys remain unverified.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/guotree/magpie-websearch/compare/v0.5.0...v0.6.0

releases.name: v0.5.0 - Five new search providers and improved reliability
releases.body:
This release adds **Moonshot, Moonshot CN, Zhipu, Z.ai, and StepFun China**, bringing the total to **13 search APIs**. It also improves HTTP error handling, Unicode text truncation, test isolation, and bilingual documentation.

### New search providers

- **Moonshot / Moonshot CN:** Standalone Basic search APIs for the international and China platforms, with snippet and full-text modes. Credentials, configuration, and caches are isolated between sites.
- **Zhipu / Z.ai:** Standalone search APIs for both platforms. Zhipu supports `search_std`, `search_pro`, Sogou, and Quark; Z.ai uses `search-prime`.
- **StepFun China:** Standalone REST search with optional programming, research, government, and business categories, plus snippet or full-text selection.

All new providers use Magpie’s credential management, search ordering, and on/off controls. They support custom complete endpoint URLs and per-provider plugin options.

### Reliability and maintenance

- Preserve known HTTP status codes and retry metadata when reading an error response body fails or times out, allowing Magpie to continue key rotation.
- Cancel unread response bodies when returning a fixed HTTP 402 error, without waiting for cleanup.
- Preserve StepFun’s `type` and `code` identifiers before truncating long error messages.
- Share Unicode text truncation across adapters, preserving surrogate pairs and avoiding full-page array allocation.
- Improve provider names in configuration errors and reduce test dependencies on unrelated providers and registration counts.

### Documentation

- Split and expand the Chinese and English technical references, covering defaults, environment variables, protocol limits, and verification records.
- Clarify the distinction between StepFun’s China REST API and its international Step Plan MCP endpoint. This release integrates China REST only.
- Add the LINUX DO friend link to both READMEs.

### Validation

- **219 tests passed** on both Node.js 24.19.0 and Bun 1.4.4.
- Isolated host checks passed on **Magpie 0.1.3026**, covering registration filters, custom endpoints, timeouts, key rotation, and fallback.
- New providers were verified with dummy keys and local mock services. Successful searches, billing, account limits, and retrieval quality with real account keys remain unverified.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/guotree/magpie-websearch/compare/v0.4.0...v0.5.0

releases.name: v0.3.0 - Parallel search and exact endpoint architecture
releases.body:
Parallel is now available as `magpie-websearch:parallel`, with anonymous search through its hosted MCP endpoint and authenticated search through its GA REST API. Leave the key empty to search without an API key; a supplied key selects REST.

## What's new in v0.3.0

### Parallel Web Search
- **Dual-mode access**: Anonymous MCP (`POST https://mcp.parallel.ai/mcp`, tool `web_search`) and authenticated REST (`POST https://api.parallel.ai/v1/search` with `x-api-key`).
- **Modes**: Defaults to `fast` mode. REST supports `fast`, `turbo`, `basic` and `advanced`; non-`fast` modes require a key.
- **Constraints & Excerpts**: Enforces Parallel's 1–200 character keyword query limit, joins multiple excerpts with double linebreaks, respects `contentChars` (default 4000 code points, 0 keeps all), preserves `publish_date` as `age`, and applies the 20-result upstream cap.
- **Fault-tolerance**: Supports anonymous 429 cooldown with `Retry-After`, and keyed refusals never fall back to anonymous mode.

### Exact Endpoint Resolution (WYSIWYG)
- **Eliminated heuristic rewriting**: Replaced `searchEndpoint` path-guessing logic with `resolveEndpoint`. Custom Base URLs are now treated as exact endpoints without appending `/v1/search` or modifying paths, eliminating proxy path pollution.
- All six providers (AnySearch, Keenable, Linkup, Parallel, Querit, TinyFish) now share a 100% symmetric, predictable endpoint model.

### Shared MCP Transport
- Generalizes stateless single-tool MCP execution and structured result extraction into `src/mcp.mjs`.
- Removed legacy transitional files, unifying provider directory structure.

## Verification
- All 94 automated tests pass on Node.js and Bun.
- Verified in Magpie 0.1.2901 sandbox: provider loading, registration filters, custom exact endpoints, timeout, 429 cooldown and fallback across all providers.

**Full changelog:** https://github.com/guotree/magpie-websearch/compare/v0.2.1...v0.3.0

releases.name: v0.2.1 - TinyFish anonymous and keyed search
releases.body:
TinyFish is now available as `magpie-websearch:tinyfish`, with anonymous search through its hosted MCP endpoint and authenticated search through its REST API. Leave the key empty to search without an API key; a supplied key selects REST.

- Support MCP JSON and SSE responses, cancellation and timeouts while reading streams, and anonymous HTTP 429 cooldowns.
- Add location, language, domain filters, search type and a local result cap. Paper search (`research_paper`) requires a key.
- Keep settings and caches isolated per plugin instance, endpoint, access mode, key and effective search parameters. A refused key does not fall back to anonymous access.
- Register all five providers by default while preserving the existing `enable`/`disable` filters.
- Scope the MCP transport to `src/providers/tinyfish-mcp.mjs` and update configuration, provider and release documentation.

TinyFish custom Base URLs are complete endpoints: no path is appended. Use an MCP endpoint without a key and a compatible REST Search endpoint with one. Leaving the address empty selects the corresponding official endpoint automatically.

Validation: all 74 tests pass on Node.js 24.19.0 and Bun 1.4.4. The real magpie 0.1.2897 host passes the smoke checks, including MCP JSON/SSE, REST GET, local caps, cooldown and fallback. Anonymous search was also verified against TinyFish's live endpoint. REST success with a real account key has not been verified; keyed requests and SSE parsing were tested against a local fake service. The anonymous quota scope and precise limits remain unverified.
